voice.persona: Two fixed companion voices (companions.md §5): Dr. Omar, lead host — male, late 30s, friendly, confident, medium-low pitch; Noor, co-host — female, early-to-mid 30s, warm, calm, clear. Neither voice may be cloned from or resemble a real employee. Provider and voice ids pending program D10.

segments.narration: NOOR: Welcome to Facility Management & Safety. You will practise decisions that help you act with confidence. You will leave with practical actions for your next shift.
segments.on_screen_text: "Facility Management & Safety" · "Your first-week safety essentials"
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: CBAHI surveyors ask staff, not just managers. On my first day I didn't know where the nearest call point was.
segments.on_screen_text: 3 icons: Protect patients · Protect you · Pass the CBAHI survey; "9 short sections · resume any time"
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: This reflection is not scored. Choose the response that helps you set one intention for your next shift.
segments.on_screen_text: "How confident are you to act in a fire right now?" 1–4
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: The chapter is a survey requirement, a shared responsibility, and one connected system.
segments.on_screen_text: Survey requirement · Everyone's responsibility · One connected system
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Open each marker in turn before you decide what happens next.
segments.on_screen_text: Icon grid of 8 plans (own SVG). Each region opens: purpose + 4 main functions
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Plans and codes are two views of the same system: give one example of each.
segments.on_screen_text: "A fire is a Code Red. A chemical spill is a Code Orange."
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Match each item to the person or step that owns it, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: 8 pairs: plan ↔ purpose (one sentence each)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Risk is likelihood plus severity. A hazard is the thing, risk is the chance it hurts someone.
segments.on_screen_text: Health · Safety · Hazard · Risk (front term, back definition + example)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: A near miss is the most valuable report: it is free learning.
segments.on_screen_text: Near miss · First aid · Medical treatment · Lost time · Fatality. Near miss tagged "most valuable to report"
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: AREC as a habit before every task, not a form.
segments.on_screen_text: Circular SVG: Anticipate → Recognise → Evaluate → Control
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Put the steps in the order you would follow at work, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Order most → least effective: Elimination, Substitution, Engineering, Administrative, PPE
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Play the situation through and decide, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Corridor with a trailing cable across a walkway near a patient waiting area (illustration). 3 nodes: (1) what do you do first; (2) which control is strongest (re-route cable / cover / sign / warn); (3) supervisor says "leave it …
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: OMAR: You can stop unsafe work without fear. If you're unsure, ask your supervisor who your liaison is.
segments.on_screen_text: Department Safety Liaison (ask your supervisor on day 1) · Right to stop unsafe work · Right to be consulted · Right to training
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: NOOR: Codes are announced overhead. Learn the meaning, then your site's extension. Code Blue is 2222 everywhere.
segments.on_screen_text: 11 cards: front = code name + colour chip (bilingual EN/AR), back = meaning + extension (pending D2)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Match each item to the person or step that owns it, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: 8 pairs (randomised): Red–Fire, Orange–Hazmat spill, White–Violent situation, Black–Bomb threat, Pink–Child/infant abduction, Blue–Cardiac arrest, Yellow–External disaster, Brown–Utility failure
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Evacuation and End of Disaster are announcements, not colours. Only stand down on the official all-clear.
segments.on_screen_text: Hospital Evacuation (go to assembly point) · End of Disaster (stand down only on this signal)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Put the steps in the order you would follow at work, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Recognise → Activate → Respond → Stand down
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: The ERT is five teams. You are part of the response even if you're not on it.
segments.on_screen_text: ERT diagram: Safety · Security · Nursing · Facility · Operation around an Incident Commander
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Remove one side of the triangle and the fire stops. Smoke kills first, which is why RACE rescues and contains before extinguishing.
segments.on_screen_text: Triangle: Heat · Fuel · Oxygen. Callout: "Smoke, not flame, is the leading cause of death."
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Put the steps in the order you would follow at work, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Rescue → Alarm → Contain → Extinguish/Evacuate
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Put the steps in the order you would follow at work, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Pull → Aim (low, at the base) → Squeeze → Sweep
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Walk the corridor. Know where these are before you need them.
segments.on_screen_text: Clinic corridor illustration with 8 regions: smoke detector, heat detector, call point, extinguisher, fire blanket, sprinkler, evacuation chair, assembly-point sign
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Place each item where it belongs, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Items: "Burning paper bin", "Petrol leak", "Smoking photocopier", "Magnesium shavings", "Pantry pan fire" → targets Class A / B / C / D / K
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Horizontal first. Vertical by stairs. Full evacuation only for the worst events.
segments.on_screen_text: Horizontal (first response, same floor) · Vertical (stairwells, never elevators) · Full (whole building, assembly point)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: "Smoke in Room 3; fire doors at the end of the corridor; patients on the same floor are not in danger yet. First move?" → Horizontal to the next compartment
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: "Oxygen is flammable." → False: oxidiser, intensifies fire
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Play the situation through and decide, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Night shift: smoke from a waste bin in a patient room. Nodes: (1) first action (rescue patient); (2) the call — what to say (code, location, ID & name); (3) contain (remove O₂ cylinder and alcohol rub, close door); (4) …
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Prevention rules exist because each item started a real fire somewhere.
segments.on_screen_text: 7 icons: candles · unauthorised welding · extensions · heaters/boilers · smoking & vaping · unauthorised microwaves · uncontrolled flammables
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Chemicals come in one door only — procurement — and never without a label and an SDS.
segments.on_screen_text: Approved procurement only · On the inventory with SDS · Never accept an unlabelled container
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Match each item to the person or step that owns it, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: 9 pairs: pictogram (own SVG via left_html image or name) ↔ hazard
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Label the parts you can name, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Place 4 labels: Health (blue) · Flammability (red) · Reactivity (yellow) · Special (white)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Diamond shows Health 3 · Flammability 0 · Reactivity 1 · Special W. "What does this tell you before opening?" → serious health hazard; do not use water
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Storage, transport and handling all follow the SDS.
segments.on_screen_text: Storage per SDS · Designated carts & routes · PPE per SDS · Flammable cabinet (double-walled, self-latching) · SDS at point of use
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: OMAR: Find your nearest eyewash today. 15 minutes feels long — don't stop early.
segments.on_screen_text: "Find your nearest one today." "Flush ≥ 15 minutes." Photo of a unit (own)
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: NOOR: Play the situation through and decide, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: 3 short cases: (a) small spill of hand rub; (b) a spill over the threshold of surface disinfectant; (c) a few mL of a highly toxic reagent → Code Orange? + 4 response steps (isolate & warn → PPE per …
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Never recap. Place each item where it belongs, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Items: used needle, blood-soaked dressing, paper towel (clean), scalpel blade, gloves with body fluid, food wrapper → General / Infectious / Sharps
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Your badge identifies you. Everyone without one in a restricted area is your concern.
segments.on_screen_text: People: ID always · contractor permits · visitor badges · Premises: CCTV · lost & found → Security · designated parking · no smoking anywhere
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: "A man without a badge is in the staff-only medication room and says he is a contractor." Best action → politely ask for permit/badge; if none, call Security; do not leave him alone
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Red sockets are on generator power. Know your shut-off valves. Isolation-room vents protect everyone.
segments.on_screen_text: Treatment-room illustration: red emergency socket (per B6), standard socket, UPS-backed monitor, unauthorised extension (crossed), water shut-off valve, HVAC vent in isolation room
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: "The isolation room is cold. A visitor asks you to close the vent." → Never disable isolation-room vents; report to Maintenance
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Labels tell you if a device is safe to use today.
segments.on_screen_text: Inspection label (date + status) · PPM schedule · "Out of Service" tag
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: OMAR: Play the situation through and decide, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: An infusion pump's label is 2 months overdue; the ward is busy. Nodes: use or not → tag out of service → who to notify (Biomedical Engineering) → colleague suggests moving a pump from another room (never relocate without BME)
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: NOOR: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: "Store cylinders upright and secured, with full and empty clearly separated." → True
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Ionising vs non-ionising. The MRI magnet is always on.
segments.on_screen_text: Ionising: X-ray, CT → dosimeters, shielding · Non-ionising: MRI, ultrasound, laser · MRI: magnet always on, screening every time · X-ray rooms: lead apron, stand behind the shield
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Match each item to the person or step that owns it, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Justification · Optimisation · Limitation ↔ definitions
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Time, distance, shielding — three levers you control.
segments.on_screen_text: Time · Distance · Shielding around a source icon
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Wear your badge. The RSO is your contact.
segments.on_screen_text: OSL dosimeter · Lead apron · RSO is your contact
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: "A quarterly OSL reading shows 2.0 mSv. What happens?" → Notification level: you are informed and monitored (values pending B4)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Match each item to the person or step that owns it, then read the feedback.

segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Laser eye injuries often don't hurt at first — that's why protection is not optional.
segments.on_screen_text: Eyes (often no pain) · Skin burns · High voltage → Eye protection · Beam management · Control reflections · Training
segments.speaker: noor
